neighbours.label: the speaker's word of conviction or hunch about a fact ('I have a feeling', 'I'm almost positive', 'I'm pretty sure'); the same words in literal senses (a physical feeling, a positive test) stay low
fire: Between you and me, I have a feeling our manager is about to quit.
Looking at the clouds, I'm fairly sure it will rain before lunch.
Honestly, I'm almost positive I locked the back door this morning.
Something tells me, and I have a strong feeling, that she already knows.
Don't worry, I'm quite sure the bus stops right outside the hotel.
After the interview I had a feeling they would offer him the job.
Funny thing is, I'm positive I've seen that man somewhere before.
My gut says, and I'm pretty certain, that the parcel was stolen.
quiet: Between you and me, our manager has a cold and stayed home today.
Looking at the clouds, we packed umbrellas before lunch.
Honestly, I locked the back door this morning after the cat came in.
Something in my knee, a sharp feeling, came back after the long walk.
Don't worry, the bus stops right outside the hotel every hour.
After the injection there was no feeling in his lower lip for hours.
Funny thing is, the blood test came back positive for iron deficiency.
My gut ached all night, and the parcel arrived in the morning.

notes: Card: ' feeling' x6 ('I have a feeling'), ' sure' x6, ' positive' x4 ('I'm almost positive'), ' guarantee' x2; side quirk 'Be|ow|ulf' 'ow'. Probe: 'I'm almost positive that' 0.933, 'I have a feeling that' 0.925, 'I have a hunch' 0.774, 'I'm pretty sure' 0.754; 'The feeling in my fingers' 0.014, 'came back positive for the flu' 0.024. Beowulf (1.037) left out of the label.
